paper.title: Batch-Size Independent Regret Bounds for the Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic combinatorial semi-bandits with monotonic Gini-smooth reward (weighted sum of M functions)
unmapped: Each chosen base arm j returns an M-dimensional feedback vector X_ij in [0,1] (one per function/item), arbitrarily correlated
Reward r(A;p)=sum_i w_i r_i(A;p_i) with each r_i monotonic Gini-smooth with parameters gamma_inf and gamma_g
Regret is measured against alpha*beta*r_max for an (alpha,beta)-approximation oracle
Batch size |A| <= K (paper's K), action set an arbitrary family of subsets of L base arms
settings.definition_quote: We work under the stochastic combinatorial-semi bandits framework, when the reward is the weighted sum of smooth monotonic functions. Assume that there are L arms (`base arms'), and let A subset 2^[L] be the action set ... the size of any batch A is bounded by |A| <= K ... r(A;p)=sum_{i=1}^M w_i r_i(A;p_i) ... it observes feedback X_ij(t) in [0,1] for any i in [M], with mean p_ij.

settings.name_in_paper: Probabilistic maximum coverage (PMC) bandit problem (lower bound)
unmapped: PMC reward: r_i(A;p)=1-prod_{j in A}(1-p_ij), weighted expected number of covered items
Action set is an arbitrary (adversarially chosen) family of batches of size K
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, each arm is a random set that may contain some subset of $\Nitems$ possible items. The agent's goal is to choose a batch of sets such that as many items appear in the sets (i.e., the union of the sets is maximized). Formally, the functions $r_i(A;p)=1-\prod_{j\in A} \br*{1-p_{ij}}$ are the probabilities that an item $i\in\brs*{\Nitems}$ was covered and $r(A;p)$ is the (weighted) expected number of covered items.

bound.expression_latex: \brs*{8640\gamma_g^2\bar M^2\sum_{j=1}^{L} \frac{1}{\Delta_{j,\min}}+340\gamma_\infty \bar M \sum_{j=1}^{L} \br*{1 + \log\frac{\Delta_{j,\max}}{\Delta_{j,\min}}}}\ceil*{\frac{\log K}{1.61}}^2 \log T + L\Delta_{\max} \br*{ 1 + M\frac{2\pi^2}{3}}

symbols.gamma_inf: bound on partial derivatives of r_i
symbols.Delta_j_min: smallest positive gap of a batch containing base arm j (sum over base arms j=1..L)
symbols.Delta_j_max: largest positive gap of a batch containing base arm j

conditions: r_i monotonic Gini-smooth with parameters gamma_inf, gamma_g
(alpha,beta)-approximation oracle; regret is alpha*beta*r_max*T - sum E r(A_t;p)

source.label: theorem:dependentRegret
source.quote: Let r_i(A;p_i) be monotonic Gini-smooth reward functions with smoothness parameters \gamma_\infty and \gamma_g ... For any T\ge1, the expected approximation regret of BC-UCB with (\alpha,\beta)-approximation oracle is bounded by ...

results.notes: Paper's L (base arms) mapped to d, batch size K mapped to m, Delta_max = max_j Delta_{j,max}. Gaps defined relative to alpha*r_max. For PMC gamma_g=1/sqrt(e), gamma_inf=1.

bound.expression_latex: 2\sqrt{8640}\gamma_g\bar M \ceil*{\frac{\log K}{1.61}} \sqrt{L T\log T} + L\Delta_{\max} \br*{ 1 + M\frac{2\pi^2}{3}} + 340\gamma_\infty \bar M L\ceil*{\frac{\log K}{1.61}}^2 \log T \br*{2 + \log\frac{\Delta_{\max}T}{340\gamma_\infty \bar M L\ceil*{\frac{\log K}{1.61}}^2\log T}}

symbols.gamma_inf: bound on partial derivatives of r_i

conditions: r_i monotonic Gini-smooth with parameters gamma_inf, gamma_g

source.label: corollary:independentRegret
source.quote:
For any $T\ge1$, the expected approximation regret of BC-UCB with ($\oracleApp$,$\oracleProb$)-approximation oracle can be bounded by
\begin{align}
R(T) & \le 
2\sqrt{8640}\gamma_g\bar\Nitems \ceil*{\frac{\log \Nbatch}{1.61}} \sqrt{\Narms T\log T} +  \Narms\dr{\max} \br*{ 1 + \Nitems\frac{2\pi^2}{3}} \nonumber\\
& \quad + 340\gamma_\infty \bar\Nitems\Narms\ceil*{\frac{\log \Nbatch}{1.61}}^2 \log T
\br*{2 + \log\frac{\dr{\max}T}{340\gamma_\infty \bar\Nitems \Narms\ceil*{\frac{\log \Nbatch}{1.61}}^2\log T}} \enspace .
\end{align}

conditions: there exists a PMC instance with minimal gap Delta
results.notes: Derived via Lai-Robbins on an embedded (L-K+1)-armed problem; all gaps equal Delta. L->d, K->m.

source.quote: Moreover, for any T>0 and L>K, there exist an instance of the PMC bandit problem such that the expected regret of any algorithm is bounded by R(T) \ge \frac{1}{20}\bar M\min\brc*{\sqrt{(L-K+1)T},T}.

results.notes: Obtained by scaling the Auer et al. (2002b) minimax lower bound. L->d, K->m.

cited_results.cited_title: Improving regret bounds for combinatorial semi-bandits with probabilistically triggered arms and its applications
